details.content: Using the five Amazon Reviews domains (Books, Electronics, Movies, CDs, Home) and the CNN architecture (three filter heights $h\in\{3,4,5\}$, 127 channels, ReLU, 1-max pooling, MLP dim 117, embedding dim 417, max seq length 500, embeddings from $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$, conv/MLP He initialization (weights from $\mathcal{U}(-b,b)$ with $b=\sqrt{6/((1+a^2)\times\text{fan\_in})}$), Adam lr $1\mathrm{e}{-3}$, $\ell_2$ weight $1\mathrm{e}{-5}$, batch size 32, dropout $p=0.285$) with iterative magnitude pruning ($p=35\%$, $r_{total}=20$), a phase transition occurs at approximately $96\%$ sparsity: beyond this threshold, subnetworks reinitialized to random draws from the original initialization distributions (TICKET-RANDOM) exhibit rapid test accuracy degradation and high instability, whereas subnetworks reinitialized to their original initial values (TICKET-RESET) maintain substantially better and more stable test accuracy, even at sparsity levels exceeding $99.9\%$.

search_documents.text: In CIFAR-10 experiments with $K=10$ class-specific subnetworks, RTL attains balanced accuracy values of 0.781, 0.778, and 0.772 at 25%, 50%, and 75% weight sparsity respectively, outperforming a single shared-mask Iterative Magnitude Pruning (IMP) baseline (0.711, 0.711, 0.732) and matching or exceeding independent per-class IMP models trained without weight sharing (0.712, 0.710, 0.760); at the same sparsity levels RTL achieves recall 0.821 / 0.810 / 0.816 versus 0.480 / 0.480 / 0.518 for the single-mask IMP baseline and 0.701 / 0.702 / 0.766 for independent per-class IMP models, while using 103K / 72K / 38K trainable parameters (RTL) compared to 944K / 629K / 314K parameters for the independent per-class models.
search_documents.title: B:2

search_documents.text: In CIFAR-100 experiments where $K=8$ semantically derived clusters are used as subsets, RTL achieves balanced accuracy 0.765 / 0.751 / 0.759 and recall 0.764 / 0.729 / 0.754 at 25% / 50% / 75% sparsity, surpassing a single-mask IMP baseline (balanced accuracy 0.722 / 0.707 / 0.742; recall 0.420 / 0.421 / 0.463) and independent-model IMP (balanced accuracy 0.712 / 0.700 / 0.744; recall 0.660 / 0.637 / 0.732) while using 108K / 76K / 40K parameters versus 944K / 629K / 314K for independent models.

search_documents.text: In implicit neural representation (INR) reconstruction experiments on 10 ADE20K images where semantic segmentation masks define within-image regions and RTL learns region-specialized subnetworks, RTL achieves higher peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) than a single-mask IMP baseline at all reported sparsity levels.
search_documents.title: B:4

search_documents.text: On a speech enhancement task constructed by mixing clean speech from the DNS-2020 dataset with noise from TAU Urban Acoustic Scenes 2020 and grouping noises into three acoustic-environment subsets (indoor, outdoor, transportation), RTL achieves higher scale-invariant signal-to-noise ratio improvement (SI-SNRi) than both a single-mask IMP baseline and independently pruned IMP models at 25% / 50% / 75% sparsity.

search_documents.text: RTL identifies a failure mode called subnetwork collapse in which aggressive pruning causes specialized subnetworks to converge toward excessive overlap in their retained weights, coinciding with sharp performance degradation.

[Referenced claim 6: RTL identifies a failure mode called subnetwork collapse in which aggressive pruning causes specialized subnetworks to converge toward excessive overlap in their retained weights, coinciding with sharp performance degradation.]

search_documents.text: In CIFAR-10, Spearman rank-order correlations between WordNet semantic proximity—semantic proximity between class labels computed via WordNet path similarity, a lexical-semantic distance metric derived from the WordNet taxonomy—and mask similarity (per-layer mask Jaccard similarity) vary with layer depth and pruning level, increasing during training and—specifically in deep layers—rising up to moderate sparsity (around 55% weight pruning) before declining at excessive sparsity.
search_documents.title: B:9

search_documents.text: In CIFAR-10, during training and with increasing weight pruning up to moderate sparsity, mask structure in deeper layers increasingly reflects high-level semantic relations between class labels, until aggressive pruning destroys the alignment between mask structure in deeper layers and high-level semantic relations between class labels.
search_documents.title: B:10

search_documents.text: In Panel B of the Figure 2 mask collapse analysis, correlations across network depth during optimization showed weak correlations that decreased with depth in early optimization but increased consistently in later epochs, particularly in middle and deep layers, indicating a gradual emergence of semantic structure as subnetworks refined specialized connectivity.

search_documents.text: In the semantic and structural correlation analysis of RTL subnetworks for four representative classes (airplane, cat, deer, and truck), semantically related classes (cat and deer) showed stronger correlations of 0.6-0.7 that grew with pruning and depth, whereas unrelated classes (airplane and truck) remained weaker at 0.2-0.3, as measured by Spearman's rank-order correlation between semantic similarity and mask similarity; this pattern indicates that RTL subnetworks for related categories preserve overlapping structures while distant ones evolve independently and is consistent with overall mask stability across dissimilar classes.
search_documents.title: B:O02

search_documents.text: For each ADE20K image (A-J) in the INR experiment, across sparsity levels, pruning of INR subnetworks showed that the sharp decline in PSNR closely coincides with the point at which mask similarity collapses, indicating that reconstruction quality degrades most significantly once subnetworks corresponding to different semantic regions begin to overlap or interfere rather than as a direct consequence of parameter removal alone, with PSNR and average mask similarity measured by the Jaccard index.
search_documents.title: B:O04

search_documents.text: For a single ADE20K image with four semantic regions, region-specific subnetworks were assessed by per-class PSNR and average mask similarity to all other region-specific subnetworks as functions of sparsity, and performance degradation coincided with a rapid increase in mask similarity, indicating subnetwork collapse at high pruning ratios.
search_documents.title: B:O05

search_documents.text: For a second ADE20K image with fifteen semantic regions, as sparsity increased in region-specific pruning masks, per-class PSNR declined gradually until a sharp drop that aligned with increasing similarity between region-specific pruning masks, reflecting loss of structural specialization.
search_documents.title: B:O06

search_documents.text: At 75% sparsity in qualitative INR reconstructions, RTL maintained more faithful structure and color consistency than IMP, which exhibited increased blurring and loss of high-frequency details, with the gap between the methods becoming more visible as sparsity increased.
search_documents.title: B:O09

search_documents.text: In qualitative speech enhancement results at 50% sparsity across different acoustic environments, RTL more effectively suppresses noise and preserves harmonic speech structure than IMP across all environments.
search_documents.title: B:O11

search_documents.text: On CIFAR-10 with class-specific subnetworks at 25%, 50%, and 75% sparsity, RTL achieved the highest balanced accuracy across all sparsity levels, significantly outperforming both baselines at 25% with 0.781 vs. 0.711 for single-model IMP and 0.712 for multi-model IMP, and remaining higher at 50% (0.778 vs. 0.711 for single-model IMP) and at 75% (0.772 vs. 0.760 for multi-model IMP), while using an order of magnitude fewer parameters.
search_documents.title: B:O12

search_documents.text: On CIFAR-10 with class-specific subnetworks at 25%, 50%, and 75% sparsity, RTL achieved the highest recall at all sparsity levels (0.821, 0.810, and 0.816), exceeding the single-model IMP baseline (0.480, 0.480, and 0.518) and matching or surpassing the multi-model alternative (0.701, 0.702, and 0.766), demonstrating that RTL subnetworks effectively preserve class-relevant signals under aggressive pruning.
search_documents.title: B:O13

search_documents.text: On CIFAR-100 with cluster-specialized subnetworks at 25%, 50%, and 75% sparsity, RTL achieved the highest balanced accuracy across all sparsity levels: 0.765 at 25%, 0.751 at 50%, and 0.759 at 75%, outperforming both baselines even at 75% sparsity, where model capacity is most constrained.
search_documents.title: B:O15

search_documents.text: On CIFAR-100 with cluster-specialized subnetworks at 25%, 50%, and 75% sparsity, RTL achieved recall values of 0.764, 0.729, and 0.754, substantially exceeding the single-model IMP baseline (0.420-0.463) and consistently outperforming the multi-model alternative, confirming that RTL subnetworks retained cluster-discriminative features more effectively under pruning.
search_documents.title: B:O16

search_documents.text: In the INR experiment on the ADE20K dataset at 25%, 50%, and 75% sparsity, RTL achieved PSNR values of 18.86, 17.25, and 14.87, respectively, versus single-model IMP's 15.94, 14.72, and 12.69, consistently outperforming IMP with advantages of almost 3 dB, 2.53 dB, and 2.18 dB, respectively.
search_documents.title: B:O17

search_documents.text: At 25%, 50%, and 75% sparsity, RTL uses only 103K, 72K, and 38K parameters, respectively, compared with 944K, 629K, and 314K for multi-model IMP—nearly 10× more—to achieve comparable accuracy.
search_documents.title: B:O18

search_documents.text: In the INR experiment on 10 ADE20K images at 25%, 50%, and 75% sparsity, RTL consistently achieved higher PSNR than the single-model IMP baseline across all samples and sparsity levels, with the gap observed for images with diverse scene content and appearance characteristics, confirming that the aggregate improvements reported in the main text are not driven by a small subset of favorable samples.

search_documents.text: Iterative magnitude pruning with layerwise magnitude selection in a binary sentiment analysis task on five Amazon Reviews domains (Books, Electronics, Movies, CDs, Home) using a CNN with three filter heights $h\in\{3,4,5\}$, each with 127 channels, ReLU activation, 1-max pooling, one hidden MLP layer of dimension 117, embedding dimension $d=417$, max sequence length $n=500$, embeddings initialized from $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ and convolutional/MLP layers initialized with He initialization, trained with Adam at learning rate $1\mathrm{e}{-3}$, $\ell_2$ weight $1\mathrm{e}{-5}$, batch size 32, dropout $p=0.285$, produces sparse subnetworks (tickets) that, when reinitialized to their original initial values (TICKET-RESET) and retrained in isolation, achieve test accuracy comparable to or better than the unpruned full model (FULL-MODEL) for moderate sparsity levels, with TICKET-RESET outperforming FULL-MODEL in the early-to-moderate sparsification regime (approximately 0%–90% sparsity) for the Books, Electronics, and Home domains.
search_documents.title: C:1

search_documents.text: In the setting of note 1, resetting the retained weights of a sparse subnetwork to random draws from the original initialization distributions (TICKET-RANDOM) yields test performance statistically similar to resetting to the original initial values (TICKET-RESET) for sparsity levels up to approximately 96%.
search_documents.title: C:2

search_documents.text: Using the five Amazon Reviews domains (Books, Electronics, Movies, CDs, Home) and the CNN architecture (three filter heights $h\in\{3,4,5\}$, 127 channels, ReLU, 1-max pooling, MLP dim 117, embedding dim 417, max seq length 500, embeddings from $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$, conv/MLP He initialization (weights from $\mathcal{U}(-b,b)$ with $b=\sqrt{6/((1+a^2)\times\text{fan\_in})}$), Adam lr $1\mathrm{e}{-3}$, $\ell_2$ weight $1\mathrm{e}{-5}$, batch size 32, dropout $p=0.285$) with iterative magnitude pruning ($p=35\%$, $r_{total}=20$), a phase transition occurs at approximately $96\%$ sparsity: beyond this threshold, subnetworks reinitialized to random draws from the original initialization distributions (TICKET-RANDOM) exhibit rapid test accuracy degradation and high instability, whereas subnetworks reinitialized to their original initial values (TICKET-RESET) maintain substantially better and more stable test accuracy, even at sparsity levels exceeding $99.9\%$.
search_documents.title: C:3

search_documents.text: The choice of initialization—whether subnetworks are reinitialized to random draws from the original initialization distributions (TICKET-RANDOM) or to their original initial values (TICKET-RESET)—is largely immaterial below approximately 96% sparsity but becomes crucial for preserving accuracy and reducing variance in the extreme-sparsity regime.
search_documents.title: C:4

search_documents.text: Under the iterative magnitude pruning procedure (prune fraction $p=35\%$, $r_{total}=20$) with the CNN architecture and training details (five Amazon Reviews domains, CNN with filters $h\in\{3,4,5\}$, 127 channels, ReLU, 1-max pooling, MLP dim 117, embedding dim 417, max seq length 500, embeddings from $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$, conv/MLP He initialization (weights from $\mathcal{U}(-b,b)$ with $b=\sqrt{6/((1+a^2)\times\text{fan\_in})}$), Adam lr $1\mathrm{e}{-3}$, $\ell_2$ weight $1\mathrm{e}{-5}$, batch size 32, dropout $p=0.285$), when sparse masks $m$ obtained from a source domain $\mathcal{D}_s$ are applied to a target domain $\mathcal{D}_t$ (with $\mathcal{D}_s \neq \mathcal{D}_t$) and the retained parameters are reinitialized either to the source-domain original values (MASKS-RESET) or to random draws from the original initialization distributions (MASKS-RANDOM), the resulting subnetworks retrain in the target domain with only modest accuracy degradation relative to tickets obtained directly in the target domain via the same procedure (TICKET-TARGET) for sparsity levels up to approximately $90\%$.
search_documents.title: C:5

search_documents.text: Across the five Amazon review domains (Books, Electronics, Movies, CDs, Home) under the lottery ticket transfer procedure masks obtained from the CDs domain and applied to any other target domain outperform the subnetworks obtained directly in that target domain and retain stronger performance even at sparsity levels exceeding $99\%$.
